clue.text: Vehicle bent on collision

parts.note: a racing car built to be bashed into its rivals, so it is literally intent on crashing

explanation.surface: A dangerous driver's car seems determined to crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' reads as 'damaged', but here it means 'determined': this vehicle is meant to collide in races.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition of a car raced on oval tracks where deliberate contact is part of the sport.

clue.text: Lecturers in ear and chest disorders

indicators.note: disorders works as a verb here, jumbling the words ear and chest

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Medical lecturers specialise in complaints of the ear and chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorders' looks like a noun for ailments, but it is the anagram signal on EAR and CHEST together.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecturers instruct students, a near synonym for those who teach.

clue.text: Vehicle owner maybe showing signs of stress

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word owner could be arranged some other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A motorist looks strained by the demands of owning a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' is the anagram signal, hinting that the vehicle's owner could be arranged differently; it rearranges the five letters that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone haggard and visibly worried by troubles looks this way: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Give up one's rights to noisy offspring

indicators.note: noisy says the word for offspring is to be heard, not read

parts.note: seed is a biblical word for descendants

explanation.surface: A parent signs away their rights over loud children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noisy' seems to describe the children, but it signals a homophone of SEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender a claim or territory formally is a direct synonym phrase.

clue.text: Where to take off when carrying a fugitive

indicators.note: carrying says the strip holds the letter A within it

parts.note: aircraft take off from a runway

explanation.surface: An escapee is caught at the airfield.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway is someone who has fled, as is a fugitive: a synonym.

clue.text: Elizabethan playgoer had basic knowledge about Goneril's end

indicators.note: about places the basic knowledge round the letter taken from Goneril

parts.note: a grounding is a basic training in a subject

indicators.note: end picks the last letter of the name Goneril

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A theatregoer in Shakespeare's day knew the basics of how King Lear's daughter Goneril dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' is a link. Goneril is a daughter in King Lear, which helps the Elizabethan surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundlings were the cheapest spectators, standing in the yard of an Elizabethan playhouse.

clue.text: Column's smear about one

indicators.note: about puts the smear round the numeral for one

parts.note: to plaster is to smear thickly
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A newspaper column smears someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column's' reads as 'column is'; 'column' looks journalistic but is architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column projecting from a wall: a kind of column.

clue.text: Revolutionary stirring giving a fool support

parts.note: git is British slang for a stupid person
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: Revolutionary agitation props up a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, especially communist, used to stir revolutionary feeling.

clue.text: Union leader forcing open revolt

indicators.note: leader picks out the first letter of Union

parts.note: prising means levering or forcing open

explanation.surface: A trade-union boss forces the start of a rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a rebellion against authority, so a synonym of revolt.

clue.text: Two boys talking to bad-tempered old woman

indicators.note: talking says the two names are heard spoken together

parts.note: Harry and Dan are two boys' names

explanation.surface: Two lads chat to a grumpy old lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, HARRY and DAN run together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a strict, belligerent or shrewish older female: a synonym.

clue.text: A German federation worker is well-provided

parts.note: Bund is German for federation or league
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A labourer in the German federal state is well off.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means plentiful, in good supply, as is something well-provided.

clue.text: Flash agency used

parts.note: a flash is a very brief moment, a second
to have a hand in something is to be the agency behind it

explanation.surface: A showy agency is putting itself to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have had a previous owner, so they are used.

clue.text: Row over popular curry in eating-place

parts.note: a din is a noisy row
in means fashionable or popular
to curry a horse is to groom it with a comb

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a popular curry in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' looks like food, but it is the verb meaning to groom a horse. 'over' places DIN above IN in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dining room is the room in a house or hotel where meals are taken.

clue.text: Expression of contempt about this celebrity

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the exclamation round

parts.note: rats! is an exclamation of disgust or scorn

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer, a synonym for a celebrity.

clue.text: A crime that's without name — it's senseless

parts.note: a sin is a wrong or crime

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: i.e. goes round the name letter

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A nameless crime is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: IE wraps N. 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means foolish, donkey-like, as something senseless is.

clue.text: Orchid section in this way is enclosed

indicators.note: is enclosed shows the word for 'in this way' sits inside the section

parts.note: an area is a section or zone
thus means in this manner

explanation.surface: Part of a greenhouse is fenced off for orchids.
explanation.definitionFit: Arethusa is a genus of orchid, named after a nymph of Greek myth.

clue.text: Inability to get off where Cain went?

definitions.text: Inability to get off where Cain went?

parts.words: Inability to get off where Cain went?
parts.note: Cain went to the land of Nod in Genesis, and the land of Nod is also slang for sleep, so this is failure to drop off

explanation.surface: Someone cannot leave for the place Cain was exiled to.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Cain dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden; 'the land of Nod' is also a jokey phrase for sleep, and 'get off' means fall asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is a chronic inability to fall asleep, cryptically described via the biblical land of Nod.

clue.text: It helps to keep a roof over one's head when everything looks black

definitions.text: It helps to keep a roof over one's head when everything looks black

parts.words: It helps to keep a roof over one's head when everything looks black
parts.note: in a coal mine everything is black, and a timber post holds up the roof of the tunnel

explanation.surface: Something keeps a person housed when times look bleak.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests financial help in dark days; the literal picture is a coal mine, where the roof needs propping.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit prop is a timber post supporting the roof of a mine working.

clue.text: An old crock

parts.note: crock in its sense of pottery: a broken fragment of an ancient pot

explanation.surface: Someone is described as a decrepit old person or car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old crock' usually means a worn-out person or vehicle; here crock is earthenware.
explanation.definitionFit: A potsherd is a fragment of broken pottery, often found by archaeologists.

clue.text: Love to have room for this instrument

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
taken as written
scope means room or space to act

explanation.surface: A lover needs space for a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' and 'for this' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An otoscope is a medical instrument used to look into the ear.

clue.text: Indisputable point -—- see holy writ

parts.note: E is a compass point, east
vide is Latin for 'see', used in references
NT is the New Testament, part of holy scripture

explanation.surface: A preacher says a point is beyond dispute: see the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plain and obvious, so not open to dispute.

clue.text: Stop ignoring the leader — soldier may be at it

indicators.note: ignoring the leader says the first letter of the word for stop is dropped

parts.note: to cease is to stop

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop disregarding the commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At ease' is a drill command letting a soldier stand relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier told to relax stands 'at ease', so the missing word fits the phrase.

clue.text: Cruising a canal in the Midlands

definitions.meaning: travelling by boat, steering a course
many English canals are named '...', such as the Trent ... in the Midlands

explanation.surface: Boating along an English waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Midlands is the central region of England, criss-crossed by canals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means steering a vessel, and is also the formal name of some canalised rivers.

clue.text: Said to be gratified here by change of leader

indicators.note: by change of leader means the first letter of the word for said is swapped for another

parts.note: rumoured means said or reported
H stands for here, as in the abbreviation for hospital or on maps

explanation.surface: Someone is reportedly pleased by a new boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' looks like a homophone signal but is the word RUMOURED.
explanation.definitionFit: To humour someone is to indulge them, so humoured means gratified.

clue.text: Emperor's gamble, losing head

indicators.note: losing head drops the first letter of the word for gamble

parts.note: a lotto is a lottery, a gamble

explanation.surface: An emperor's bet fails and he loses his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emperor's' is read as 'Emperor is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors, such as Otto the Great.

clue.text: Cheeky in manner, sent back to warehouse

indicators.note: sent back reverses the whole combination
in puts the cheeky word inside the manner

parts.note: tone means manner or style
pert means saucy or cheeky

explanation.surface: Someone cheeky in manner is dispatched to a storehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns the whole container round, so 'Cheeky in manner' is read from right to left to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a port or warehouse where goods are stored for re-export.

clue.text: One to aim at? Hit it spot on

indicators.note: hit means struck, so the letters of the next words are knocked about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A target to aim for: hit it right in the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' looks like part of the advice, but it is the anagram signal on IT SPOT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A spittoon is a receptacle that people spit into, so one aims at it: whimsical.

clue.text: Entrance to theatre circle jammed outside — it should work both ways

indicators.note: entrance to picks the first letter of theatre
outside means the jammed word goes round the circle

parts.note: wedged means jammed tightly
O is a circle shape

explanation.surface: The theatre's dress circle is packed with people outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circle' suggests the theatre's balcony but just gives the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-edged argument or blade cuts both ways, having two effects.
